chunks: That ʿAlī عليه السلام cut off the grave-robber, so it was said to him, “Do you cut off for the dead?” He said, “Indeed, we cut for our dead just as we cut for our living.”

key_terms.عَلِيّاً: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the authority issuing and applying the ruling
key_terms.قَطَعَ: cut off; referring here to the legal punishment of amputation for theft
key_terms.لِأَحْيَائِنَا: for our living; showing equivalence in legal protection
key_terms.لِأَمْوَاتِنَا: for our dead; indicating legal protection for the deceased
key_terms.نَبَّاشَ: the grave-robber; one who exhumes graves to steal

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment applied for stealing from the dead, such as grave robbery?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام applied the hadd punishment to one who robbed a grave. It shows that the property and sanctity connected to the dead are legally protected, just as they are for the living.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ordered the hand of a grave robber to be cut off.
Imam (as) was asked: "Do you cut off (the hand) for stealing from the dead?"
Imam (as) replied: "We cut for our dead just as we cut for our living."
